important.name: Junction to an ancestor sends the run-log scan into unbounded recursion
important.summary:
rglob on 3.11 descends any entry with is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) true, and a Windows junction counts as a plain directory (that is why the alias test works on Windows). A junction to the folder or an ancestor (logs/loop -> logs) recurses until the path is too long or the recursion limit is hit; the OSError or RecursionError escapes the generator, not resolved_log, so main ends in a traceback, not a problem: line. The scan survives file loops only; containment filters what is listed, not what is walked.

Also (system_shape): The module docstring (lines 5-6), check-runlogs SKILL.md line 22, the README key row for runlogs.dir and the schema description of runlogs.dir all say only dated subfolders (archived logs) are searched. find_runlogs runs folder.rglob('*') (line 63), so any subfolder at any depth is scanned, whatever its name. A log-named file in a non-dated folder such as logs/runs/scratch/ can become the 'newest' log, which none of the four documents warns about.

Also (overall, runtime): find_runlogs walks folder.rglob('*') (line 63). On Python 3.11 under Windows, rglob descends into junctions (is_symlink() is False for them), so a junction pointing at the run-log folder or an ancestor recurses until scandir raises OSError (reproduced: OSError [WinError 1921] from list(d.rglob('*')) with d/loop -> d). The error is raised by the walk itself, outside resolved_log's try block, and main() catches only RunLogError/ConfigError, so the skill gets a traceback instead of a 'problem:' line. The fcc44f9 commit and the resolved_log docstring promise that link loops never abort the scan; the only loop test (test_symlink_loop_never_aborts_the_scan) covers file symlinks, not a directory loop.

Also (runtime): find_runlogs walks with folder.rglob('*'). On Python 3.11, pathlib's _iterate_directories swallows only PermissionError. Any other OSError from scandir propagates out of find_runlogs, and main() catches only RunLogError/ConfigError, so the user gets a traceback where a 'problem:' line belongs. Two ways to hit it: a dated subfolder removed or rotated mid-scan raises FileNotFoundError, and a Windows directory junction gets descended anyway (DirEntry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) is True for junctions on 3.11). A junction loop recurses until the path gets too long. A junction that points outside the folder also makes the scan list external trees: the files get filtered, but the walk still pays for them. The 'survive link loops' hardening covers only resolve() loops inside resolved_log, not the traversal.

Also (runtime): parse_args accepts any int for --count, whose help text reads 'print the N newest logs'. newest() then returns logs[:max(args.count, 1)], so --count 0 or --count -3 prints one log with no warning. That contradicts the flag's own contract and hides a caller error.
fix: Walk explicitly (os.walk(followlinks=False) or an os.scandir stack), skipping directories whose resolved path is outside base or already visited; add a test linking LOGS/loop -> LOGS via _dir_link
At minimum catch OSError and RecursionError around the scan and raise RunLogError
Reword the four descriptions to 'subfolders at any depth (e.g. dated archive folders) are searched too'.
Or restrict the recursion to subfolders whose name carries a YYYY-MM-DD date and add a test with a non-dated subfolder.

Replace rglob with an explicit walk (os.scandir recursion or os.walk) that resolves each directory, skips one already visited or outside base, and swallows OSError per entry; add a test using _dir_link(root / LOGS / 'loop', root / LOGS) that expects the real log printed once and rc 0.
Minimum: wrap the rglob iteration in try/except (OSError, RecursionError) and raise RunLogError naming the folder, plus the same junction-loop test asserting a 'problem:' line.
Wrap the rglob loop in find_runlogs in try/except (OSError, RecursionError) and re-raise as RunLogError(f'cannot scan {folder.as_posix()}: {exc}').

Replace rglob with os.walk(folder, onerror=...) and prune any dirname whose Path.resolve() is outside base or already visited (keep a set of real directory paths). That skips junction loops and out-of-folder junctions on 3.11.
Reject N < 1 at parse time: use a small positive-int type function for --count that raises argparse.ArgumentTypeError, then slice logs[:args.count].

important.name: find-polluter.sh reports 'all tests clean' when the pattern matches no test file
important.summary:
When find returns nothing, TOTAL=0, the loop skips its single empty line, and the script prints 'No polluter found - all tests clean!' with exit 0 (lines 38-45, 89-94). That is the same false clean signal the PR removed for a missing runner (exit 126/127 -> 2): a mistyped pattern, or a '**/' pattern find cannot match, reads as a successful bisection. test_find_polluter.py has no zero-match case.

Also (roast): With zero matches TOTAL=0, the loop never runs, and the script prints No polluter found - all tests clean! and exits 0. This PR already removed the same false clean result for a missing runner and a pre-existing target; a clean verdict after zero tests proves nothing.

Also (runtime): When the pattern matches nothing (a typo, an absolute pattern, a pattern meant for another base dir), TOTAL is 0 and the loop body never runs. The script still prints 'No polluter found - all tests clean!' and exits 0, so a pattern mistake looks like a clean bisection result. Every other unusable-input case (target already present, runner missing) exits 2.
fix: After computing TOTAL, add: if [ "$TOTAL" -eq 0 ]; then echo "No test files match: $TEST_PATTERN"; exit 2; fi  and add a test asserting returncode 2 and no 'No polluter found' for a pattern that matches nothing.
Exit 2 with a no-test-files-match message when TOTAL is 0, plus a test asserting returncode 2 and no clean verdict
After computing TOTAL, if it is 0, print 'No test files match: $TEST_PATTERN' and exit 2, before the pollution-target check.

minor.name: Schema says the date group is required, but config load never checks it
minor.summary:
harness.schema.json describes runlogs.name_pattern as 'named group date (YYYY-MM-DD) required'. The schema only applies $defs/regex (format: regex, minLength 1), so a pattern with no date group passes load_config. The problem only shows up when check-runlogs runs (compile_pattern, latest_runlog.py lines 38-39). tests.file_pattern and the other regex keys are rejected at load, so this key is less strict than the description suggests.

Also (roast): The schema description calls the date group required, but only format: regex is enforced; a pattern without it loads cleanly and fails only when check-runlogs runs compile_pattern. Other config errors surface at load_config.

Also (overall): The schema description says the named group date is required, and README says the same, but the schema only checks format regex; a pattern without (?P<date>...) loads cleanly and fails only when check-runlogs runs (compile_pattern, latest_runlog.py:38-39). Config errors otherwise surface at load time (tests/lib/test_config.py invalid-config cases).
fix: Change the schema description to say check-runlogs, not config load, enforces the date group.

Or check for the date group in config.py _build (raise ConfigError when the compiled pattern has no 'date' in groupindex) and add {'runlogs': {'name_pattern': 'run_\d+\.txt'}} to test_invalid_config_raises.
Add a schema pattern requiring the named date group and a matching bad case in test_invalid_config_raises
Check the group in _build and raise ConfigError
Check the date group in the RunLogsConfig builder in config.py (raise ConfigError) and add {'runlogs': {'name_pattern': 'run_\d+\.txt'}} to test_invalid_config_raises.
Or reword the schema description to say the group is checked when check-runlogs runs.

minor.name: Docs say 'dated subfolders' are searched; the scan walks every subfolder at any depth
minor.summary: check-runlogs/SKILL.md:22-23, the README key table (README.md:101) and the latest_runlog.py module docstring (lines 5-6) all say 'dated subfolders under it (archived logs) are searched too'. find_runlogs (latest_runlog.py:63) uses folder.rglob('*') with no dated-name filter, so any nested folder (e.g. a per-tool or scratch subfolder holding a log-named file) competes for 'newest'. A developer reading the docs would not expect a non-dated subfolder to supply the log handed to the investigator.
fix: Reword the three places to 'every subfolder under it (dated archives included) is searched too'.
Or restrict the walk to subfolders whose names parse as dates, and keep the current wording.

minor.name: Usage error shares exit 1 with 'polluter found'
minor.summary:
The missing-arguments branch exits 1, and so does the FOUND POLLUTER branch. The other error paths (target pre-exists, runner exit 126/127) exit 2. A caller that branches on the exit code cannot tell a usage error from a found polluter.

Also (overall): The script now distinguishes 0 (clean), 1 (polluter found) and 2 (cannot run), but the usage branch also exits 1 (line 14), so a caller keying on the exit code reads a missing argument as a found polluter. test_usage_without_arguments pins the ambiguous 1.

Also (system_shape): The script now has a three-way exit contract: 0 clean, 2 for refusals (existing target, runner missing), and 1 for a found polluter (line 85). A usage error also exits 1 (line 14), so a caller cannot tell a bad invocation from a found polluter. Neither the script header nor root-cause-tracing.md lines 109-111 documents the exit codes.

Also (roast): Could-not-bisect cases now exit 2, but a usage error still exits 1, the same code as a found polluter, so a caller cannot tell found-it from called-it-wrong.
fix: Change the usage branch's 'exit 1' to 'exit 2', and add a header comment naming the codes: 0 clean, 1 polluter found, 2 unusable input.
Change the usage branch to exit 2 and update test_usage_without_arguments to expect 2.
Or document the exit codes in the header comment and keep usage on a distinct code.
Make the usage error exit 2 and list the codes in the header comment ('exit 0 clean, 1 polluter found, 2 could not bisect'), then update test_usage_without_arguments to expect 2.
Exit 2 on the usage branch and update test_usage_without_arguments

minor.name: find-polluter '**/' collapse and './' strip are untested
minor.summary:
find-polluter.sh:31-37 documents two pattern rewrites: it strips a leading './', and it collapses '**/' so 'src/**/*.test.ts' also matches files directly under src/. Every test uses the flat pattern 't/*_test.py', so neither rewrite runs and a regression in either would not be caught.

Also (roast): Every test uses t/*_test.py; nothing covers the ./ strip or the **/ collapse at find-polluter.sh:33-37, the change most likely to regress quietly into Found 0 test files.
fix: Add a test that lays out t/top_test.py and t/sub/b c_test.py, runs with pattern 't/**/*_test.py', and asserts 'Found 2 test files' and the spaced polluter. Add a parametrized case with './t/*_test.py' for the strip.
Add a test with t/top_test.py and t/sub/deep_test.py and pattern ./t/**/*_test.py, asserting Found 2 test files

minor.name: Cwd-resolution test cannot show cwd beats CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
minor.summary:
latest_runlog.py:9-10 documents that without --repo the cwd's checkout wins and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is only the fallback. test_without_repo_the_cwd_checkout_is_used deletes CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so it would still pass if that precedence were reversed.

Also (tests): The module docstring says each test 'runs main in-process with --repo', but test_without_repo_the_cwd_checkout_is_used calls module.main([]) without it.

minor.name: Directory-link tests pass vacuously on POSIX
minor.summary: On Python 3.11, Path.rglob descends with entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False), so a symlinked directory is never entered on Linux. On the Ubuntu CI leg, _dir_link makes a real symlink, so test_linked_directory_escaping_the_folder_is_skipped and test_linked_directory_alias_lists_each_log_once pass whether or not resolved_log's escape check and find_runlogs' dedup work. They only test those paths on Windows, where the link is a junction and rglob does descend into it.
fix: Assert the precondition before running main: skip with a stated reason when `(root / LOGS).rglob('*')` yields nothing under the linked directory, so the POSIX leg reports a skip instead of a vacuous pass.
Or mark both tests skipif(os.name != 'nt') with a reason naming rglob's no-follow behaviour; the file-symlink tests already cover escape and dedup on POSIX.

minor.name: PROVENANCE row for strap-debugging omits five SKILL.md edits beyond the two it lists
minor.summary:
docs/PROVENANCE.md:16 says the import is 'Verbatim except: the SKILL.md frontmatter name/description and "(when installed)" on its two superpowers: skill pointers'. Compared with the upstream systematic-debugging/SKILL.md (identical in every locally cached release, 5.0.7 and 5.1.0), the bundled SKILL.md also: drops the Overview opener 'Random fixes waste time and create new bugs...' (upstream line 10, gone before SKILL.md:10); rewrites the Layer 1/Layer 2 env-var probes (SKILL.md:91 and :95; upstream `${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}` and `env | grep IDENTITY`, both of which echo the secret value); adds a new Phase 4 step 3 bullet pointing at superpowers:verification-before-completion (SKILL.md:189) that upstream only listed under 'Related skills'; renames 'Ultrathink this' to 'Ultra-think this' (SKILL.md:239); and deletes the trailing 'Related skills' and 'Real-World Impact' sections (after SKILL.md:283). The second 'superpowers: pointer' the row mentions does not exist upstream in that position; it was moved, not annotated. The project rule makes PROVENANCE the map from every imported file back to its source, so a future re-sync against upstream would silently revert the secret-leak fix and the moved pointer.

Also (system_shape): PROVENANCE.md line 16 lists the ways find-polluter.sh differs from upstream: paths read whole, an optional test command, a stop on 126/127, and refusing an existing target. The head script has more changes that are not listed: a non-zero-exit tally with its 'Note: N of M test files exited non-zero' line (lines 55, 70, 90-92), stdin redirected from /dev/null for each test run (line 65), and the 'To investigate' hints echoing the configured command with a quoted file (lines 83-84). Comparing against the import commit 40a9d58 confirms these lines arrived after the verbatim import.

Also (roast): Against upstream the script also strips a leading ./ from the pattern, adds a **/-collapsed -path, tallies non-zero test exits, feeds tests stdin from /dev/null and accepts 2+ arguments. None of it is listed, and the list presents itself as complete.
fix: Extend the 'Verbatim except' clause on docs/PROVENANCE.md:16 to list: Overview opener removed; Layer 1/2 env-var probes rewritten so a set secret is never echoed; the verification-before-completion pointer moved from 'Related skills' into Phase 4 step 3; 'Ultrathink' spelled 'Ultra-think'; 'Related skills' and 'Real-World Impact' sections dropped.
Or restore those SKILL.md passages to upstream text (keeping only the documented exceptions) so the row stays accurate.

Add to the find-polluter.sh clause in PROVENANCE.md: 'counts and reports test files that exited non-zero, runs each test with stdin from /dev/null, and its investigate hints echo the configured command'.
Add those deviations to the find-polluter.sh clause of the strap-debugging row

minor.name: --dir override test never sets a config value to override
minor.summary: test_dir_flag_overrides_the_config builds the project with make_project(None), so runlogs.dir is unset and the only folder available is the --dir one. The test name claims --dir beats the configured folder, but the resolve_folder precedence (`rel = flag or configured`, latest_runlog.py:89) could be reversed to `configured or flag` and this test would still pass.
fix: Build the project with {"runlogs": {"dir": LOGS}} plus a newer log under LOGS (e.g. _RUN_TESTS_2026-10-14_120000.txt) and an older log under other/; run with --dir other and assert the output is only the other/ log.

minor.name: The unrelated.bin case of test_entry_that_cannot_resolve_is_skipped cannot fail
minor.summary:
stamp() runs before resolved_log(), and unrelated.bin never matches the name pattern, so the patched Path.resolve is never called for it. The case passes even with the try/except in resolved_log deleted; only the log-named case tests the claim.

Also (tests): test_nothing_is_moved_or_written snapshots only relative paths, so a regression that rewrites, truncates or touches an existing log (content or mtime) goes unnoticed. The module docstring promises 'nothing is moved or written'. test_root_separation._snapshot already uses (size, mtime_ns) for the same kind of check.
fix: Drop unrelated.bin from the parametrize list
Replace it with a log-named entry whose resolve raises OSError, so both caught exception types are exercised
Snapshot `{relative path: (st_size, st_mtime_ns)}` for each file before and after, and assert the two dicts are equal.
